other_conditions: Eligible agencies include State Governments and UT Administrations.
Institutions or organisations set up by the Government as autonomous bodies, or societies registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
Educational and other institutions of local bodies and cooperative bodies are eligible.
A public trust registered under any law and having at least three years of registration is eligible.
Any private recognised institution conducting vocational courses for at least three years is eligible.
Industries or industry associations (e.g., ASSOCHAM, CII, FICCI) willing to run skill‑upgradation training centres are eligible.

Voluntary organisations/NGOs must be registered for at least three years, have at least three years experience in the relevant field, and demonstrate aptitude and experience in welfare work for Scheduled Tribes.
Preference is given to programmes that benefit Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PTGs) or remote/interior/backward areas not serviced by government institutions or established NGOs.
Applicants must demonstrate financial viability, good reputation, and capability to mobilise the community.
A minimum of 33% of seats must be reserved for tribal girl candidates.
benefits_summary: Grants are provided to set up and run vocational training centres and to support training of Scheduled Tribe youth, covering stipends, tools, and infrastructure costs.
documents_required: Rent Assessment Certificate issued by the State Public Works Department
